title: A rookie line that climbed out of a June hole: .264 / .662 OPS / .294 wOBA
subtitle: Cumulative by plate appearance, regular season, against the 8 other Phillies primary centre-field seasons of the Statcast era (CX-1: >80 games in CF, CF games only, so his line runs 464 of 465 PA). Bottom on June 13 (PA 210): BA .227, wOBA .274. At 465 PA he ranks 7th of 9 in BA and 8th in wOBA.

title: The turn was a June-to-August surge, not a new level
subtitle: Rolling wOBA bottomed at .205 on Jun 18 and peaked at .345 on Aug 09, then gave most of it back. A June 1 split gains only +0.014 wOBA (182 vs 283 PA); 4 of 10 candidate breakpoints show any gain (RC-5).

title: TR-1 verdict: NO TURN. Batting average turned; the skills did not
subtitle: Ten signatures registered in the BID before any split was computed; pre = Mar 26-May 31 (182 PA), post = Jun 1-Sep 27 (283 PA). Results UNSUPPORTED, process UNSUPPORTED. BABIP .285 → .336 carried the BA gain; walks went the wrong way (CONTRA) and chase did not move.

title: The profile, scored: elite bat-to-ball, a chase habit, and the flattest swing in the house
subtitle: Percentile = better than X% of 220 Phillies hitter-seasons 2015-2026 (≥50 PA; launch angle n=189, bat tracking 2024+ n=31). Lower is better for chase, whiff, K% and GB%; swing rate is shown raw (no good direction). Red = top third, navy = bottom third. Value at right.

title: He swings like a hitter who expects to make contact, because he does
subtitle: UC22 attack regions (ball width 0.25 ft, per-pitch zone). Crawford swings at 32% of chase/waste pitches (house 27%) and 58% just off the edge (house 52%), yet whiffs on only 34% of those chase swings (house 53%). House = other Phillies hitters, 2026.

title: Ground balls never let go: 58.9% GB rate, 35.1% hard-hit
subtitle: Cumulative by plate appearance vs the CX-1 centre-field seasons. Hard contact was mid-pack (4th of 9 at matched volume); the grounders were not (8th of 9, lower is better). Mean launch angle 0.9° against 13.1° for the rest of the 2026 Phillies; average attack angle 1.7°, lowest of 31 tracked Phillies seasons.

title: Where the walks went: righty spin below the zone, righty heat above it
subtitle: Out-of-zone pitches from RHP, catcher's view; coloured dots are chases. He chases RHP breaking balls (47%) and changeups (44%), far above the house chase median (31%), but the costliest chases by volume are elevated fastballs. CC-1 = runs given up versus the house take in the same count: 29.0 of his 34.3 came against righties.

title: Righty spin: the hangers stopped coming, and so did the hard contact
subtitle: RHP breaking balls (SL/ST/CU/KC). Hard-hit 45% in AAA 2025 → 32% in MLB 2026; average EV 89.7 → 87.4 mph; chase 38% → 47%. In AAA most of his hits came on breaking balls left in the heart (dotted box); in MLB only a few did. AAA is a supporting tier (different level, 25 untracked BIP). Stars = extra-base hits.

title: Against righty spin he still pulls: 56% to right field, against 33% on everything else
subtitle: Balls in play against RHP breaking balls, schematic field at CBP dimensions (329-374-401-369-330). Dotted lines are the house DR-1 pull/straightaway/oppo boundaries; shares are of classifiable BIP. On everything else his hits already go the other way (43% of 2026 hits went oppo). Stars = extra-base hits.

title: Centre field: about 10 outs short of what the ball flight said, and the notebook's method could not see it
subtitle: XO-2 proxy: 449 air balls ≥150 ft within 15° of dead centre with him in CF, each scored by the out share of similar balls (EV ±3, LA ±2, distance ±10 ft, direction ±10°) in 15,240 house comparisons. 261 outs vs 270.8 expected = -9.8, 6th of 9 Phillies CF seasons since 2015. Every neighbourhood variant is negative (-2.9 to -9.8). External: −8 OAA, −2 DRS (CI-2). No catch probability in the log; read the rank and the sign, not the decimal.
